legal_basis.to: Ordinance 6074, introduced 2026-04-06 by Legislator Sean E. Smith (120-day version); a competing 365-day version (Ordinance 6087, sponsored by Legislative Chair Manny Abarca) was also considered in committee as of 2026-06-01. The full County Legislature passed a 180-day moratorium on data-center and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) land-use applications by an 8-1 vote (one member excused) on 2026-06-22. Per KCTV5, the ordinance then went to County Executive Phil LeVota, who had 10 days to sign or veto; no veto was reported in subsequent coverage found in this pass, but the Executive's signature was not independently confirmed, and the exact ordinance/file number of the version that received final passage (whether an amended Ordinance 6074 or a substitute) was not confirmed from a primary Legistar record, which returned an access error to automated fetch.

decisions.notes: This moves the record from 'pending' to 'active': the County Legislature passed a 180-day data-center/BESS moratorium 8-1 on 2026-06-22, an increase from the originally proposed 120-day Ordinance 6074. However, two facts could not be pinned down from a primary source in this pass, so confidence is capped at 0.65 rather than higher: (1) whether the final measure was formally an amended Ordinance 6074 or a distinct file (a competing 365-day Ordinance 6087 was also in play as of June 1), and (2) whether County Executive Phil LeVota actually signed it (KCTV5 reported a 10-day sign-or-veto window running from June 22, i.e., to roughly July 2, 2026, well before this 2026-07-31 research date, and no veto was reported in later coverage, but that is an inference, not a confirmed fact). Jackson County's own Legistar portal and jacksongov.org returned errors/403 to automated fetch, preventing direct confirmation. A follow-up pass with authenticated or manual access to Jackson County's Legistar system is recommended to nail down the final ordinance number and executive-action date.
